skill.name: nextjs-devtools
skill.description: MCP helper for inspecting Next.js routes, components, build information, and Next.js configuration.
skill.summary: Inspect and debug Next.js applications through a Next.js DevTools MCP server.
skill.author: 92Bilal26

security_audit.summary: The skill provides legitimate Next.js MCP inspection features, but it includes real execution risk. The highest risk is the stdio transport using shell=True with a caller-supplied command, plus repeated unpinned npx @latest execution guidance. Most Markdown backtick and system reconnaissance alerts are false positives.

remediation.issue: Caller-supplied stdio command runs through shell=True.
remediation.suggestion: Parse stdio commands into an argument list and call subprocess.Popen with shell=False. Prefer an allowlist for supported MCP server commands.

remediation.issue: The skill runs next-devtools-mcp through an unpinned @latest package reference.
remediation.suggestion: Pin next-devtools-mcp to a reviewed version and document the expected package source. Avoid automatic upgrades during agent execution.

remediation.issue: HTTP MCP mode can send parameters and headers to a user-provided endpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before sending secrets in headers or parameters. Default documentation should use trusted localhost endpoints only.

content.value_statement: Next.js projects can be hard to inspect when routes, components, and build settings are spread across the app. This skill connects Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to a Next.js DevTools MCP server for focused project inspection.
actual_capabilities: Connects to a Next.js DevTools MCP server through stdio or HTTP.
Lists Next.js app routes and requests details for a selected route.
Lists React components discovered by the MCP server.
Reads build information exposed by the MCP server.
Reads Next.js configuration details from the connected project.
Can emit MCP tool documentation for review or caching.
limitations: Supports Next.js projects only, not general React applications.
Requires Node.js, npx, Python 3, and the Next.js DevTools MCP package.
The stdio mode and helper script execute local shell commands.
Results depend on the MCP server and the current project state.

use_cases.title: Inspect Routing During Feature Work
use_cases.description: List routes and review details before changing navigation or API handlers.

use_cases.title: Debug Build Configuration
use_cases.description: Check build information and Next.js config while investigating build or deployment issues.

use_cases.title: Map Project Structure for AI Assistance
use_cases.description: Give an AI coding tool structured route and component context before making edits.

prompt_templates.title: List Project Routes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Next.js DevTools MCP skill to list the routes in this project. Summarize the main app areas.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the route I name and explain its available details. Point out anything that may affect routing behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Check Build Settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the MCP server to review build information and Next.js configuration. Summarize likely causes of build problems.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Inspection Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect routes, components, build information, and configuration. Produce a prioritized investigation plan for a Next.js refactor.

output_examples.input: List the routes in my Next.js app.
output_examples.output: The assistant returns a concise route inventory grouped by app area, with notes about dynamic routes and API handlers.

output_examples.input: Check why my production build behaves differently.
output_examples.output: The assistant summarizes build settings and Next.js config values that may affect production behavior.

output_examples.input: Find components related to the dashboard.
output_examples.output: The assistant lists matching components and explains how they relate to the dashboard route area.

best_practices: Run the skill from the root of a trusted Next.js project.
Review the MCP server command before allowing an agent to execute it.
Pin package versions when using this skill in shared or production workflows.
anti_patterns: Do not run the helper script in an untrusted repository.
Do not send sensitive headers to an MCP server you do not control.
Do not use the skill for non-Next.js React projects.

faq.question: What does this skill inspect?
faq.answer: It inspects routes, route details, components, build information, and Next.js configuration exposed by the MCP server.

faq.question: Does it modify my Next.js project?
faq.answer: The listed MCP tools are inspection focused. The helper commands still start local processes.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it need network access?
faq.answer: It can connect to a local or user-provided HTTP MCP endpoint. Stdio mode can run npx to start a server.

faq.question: Is it safe to run automatically?
faq.answer: Use confirmation before execution because the skill can run shell commands and an unpinned npm package.

faq.question: Can it inspect any React app?
faq.answer: No. It is designed for Next.js applications and depends on Next.js DevTools MCP support.
